info.title: Chat SPX API
info.description:
Referência completa da API do **Chat SPX**.

Autentique-se enviando o header `api_access_token` (obtido no perfil do usuário ou via console). A maioria dos endpoints é escopada por conta: `/api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/...`.

tags.name: Conversations & Messages
tags.description: Manage conversations and their messages on Chat SPX: list/search/filter conversations, create them from a contact + inbox, read and update status/priority/assignment, snooze and mute, mark read/unread, manage labels, participants, per-user chat settings and drafts; send, edit, delete, retry, translate and forward messages, share location and contact cards, list media attachments, and drive the password-protected Private Chat. Conversations are addressed by their per-account numeric display id; messages by their primary key id.

tags.name: Message Engagement, Attachments & Search
tags.description: Engage with individual messages (emoji reactions, stars/bookmarks and collective pins), upload files to Chat SPX (per-conversation direct uploads and account-level blob uploads), browse and bulk-download the shared media gallery, and run full-text search across conversations, messages, contacts and help-center articles. All endpoints are account-scoped and authenticated with a user/agent access token.

tags.name: Contacts, Companies & Funnels (CRM)
tags.description: Manage the Chat SPX CRM domain: contacts (people you talk to), their notes, labels, conversations, channel links (contact inboxes) and outbound calls; companies (organizations contacts belong to); contact merges and bulk actions; and the Kanban-style sales pipeline composed of funnels, funnel stages and funnel items. Contacts are the core record of every person reachable across channels, while funnels let teams track conversations as deals moving through stages. All endpoints are account-scoped and authenticated with a user API access token (`api_access_token` header). Companies and contact calls require the Enterprise edition.

tags.name: Captain (AI Assistants & Copilot)
tags.description: Manage Chat SPX Captain - AI Assistants, their knowledge base (documents and curated Q&A responses), scenarios, custom tools, inbox connections and operational preferences (LLM provider keys, per-feature model selection). Also covers the agent-facing Copilot (threads, messages, in-conversation copilot chat and ghost reply suggestions) and the Captain Tasks helpers (rewrite, summarize, reply/label suggestions, follow-up and sentiment analysis). Enterprise feature; most write endpoints require a configured LLM (OpenAI) API key on the account.

tags.name: Reports & Analytics
tags.description: Aggregated and real-time analytics for a Chat SPX account: historical conversation time-series, period summaries with traffic-light signals, per-entity summary reports (agent, team, inbox, label, channel), live in-service dashboards, bot performance, downloadable CSV reports, raw reporting events, audit logs, per-agent personal stats, the Year in Review, and asynchronous PDF exports (conversation transcripts and report snapshots).

tags.name: Agents, Teams, Roles & Assignment
tags.description: Manage the people side of a Chat SPX account: human agents and their roles, automation agent bots, teams and their membership, granular custom roles (Enterprise), agent capacity policies with per-inbox conversation limits (Enterprise), and the assignment policies (Assignment V2) that govern how conversations are auto-distributed across agents and inboxes. Most endpoints require an administrator-level user API token. Authentication and authorization failures are surfaced as HTTP 401 by the global exception handler.

tags.name: Automation, Macros, SLA & Settings
tags.description: Account-level configuration and productivity resources for Chat SPX. Covers automation rules (event-driven if/then conditions and actions), macros (reusable batches of actions agents run on a conversation), SLA policies and the applied-SLA tracking/metrics they generate, canned responses (reply snippets with optional attachments), custom attribute definitions, saved custom filters, conversation labels, dashboard apps (embedded iframes) and inbox working-hours. All endpoints are scoped to an account and authenticated with a user access token. SLA endpoints (sla_policies, applied_slas) require an Enterprise plan.

tags.name: Help Center & Portals
tags.description: Manage the Chat SPX Help Center knowledge base. A **portal** is a public help center site (with its own slug, branding, custom domain and supported locales). Each portal groups **categories**, and each category groups **articles**. Use these endpoints to build and maintain self-service documentation: create portals and configure their look and locales, organize content into categories (including parent/child and cross-locale associations), and author, publish, archive and re-order articles. Portals are addressed in the URL by their **slug** (a string), while categories and articles are addressed by their numeric **id**. Listing portals/articles and reading a single portal is available to any agent in the account; all create, update, delete, re-order and portal-administration actions require an **administrator** API token.

tags.name: CSAT, NPS & Surveys
tags.description: Collect and analyze customer feedback in Chat SPX. This domain covers NPS (Net Promoter Score) survey responses and metrics, CSAT (Customer Satisfaction) survey responses and metrics, WhatsApp CSAT template management (create/inspect/AI utility analysis), and the public CSAT survey page that contacts use to submit a rating and feedback for a conversation.

tags.name: Campaigns & Scheduled Messages
tags.description: Endpoints for outbound automation in Chat SPX: marketing/automation **campaigns**, **scheduled messages** (queue a message on a conversation for future delivery), and **WhatsApp Cloud API message templates** (HSM). Campaigns come in two flavors derived from the inbox type: `ongoing` (website campaigns triggered by visitor rules) and `one_off` (single SMS/WhatsApp blasts). For WhatsApp, the native blaster is disabled and one-off campaigns act as an anchor/record for the SPX orchestrator (pacing, round-robin assignment, template rotation); the read-only `stats` endpoint aggregates delivery and reply metrics for that blast. Scheduled messages let an agent queue a text and/or attachments on a conversation to be sent at a future time, with pending/sent/failed/cancelled lifecycle. Message templates let you create, list and delete approved WhatsApp templates straight against the Meta Graph API without opening the WhatsApp Manager.

tags.name: Inboxes & Channels
tags.description: Manage inboxes (the entry points through which conversations reach Chat SPX) and their underlying provider channels. Create, list, configure and delete inboxes; manage inbox agent membership and the bot assigned to an inbox; connect WhatsApp numbers through WAHA sessions (QR pairing, connect/disconnect/restart); provision Twilio SMS/WhatsApp channels; register Facebook/Instagram pages; sync WhatsApp message templates; check WhatsApp Cloud channel health; and start OAuth authorization flows for WhatsApp Cloud, Instagram, Twitter (X), TikTok, Microsoft and Google. Most write operations and provider connections require an administrator API key.

tags.name: Integrations & Webhooks
tags.description: Connect Chat SPX to third-party services and stream events out. This domain covers the integration App catalog and per-account/per-inbox Hooks, first-class integrations (Slack, Linear, Shopify, Dyte, Notion, OpenAI), account Webhook subscriptions (HMAC-signed event delivery), the inbound Slack events callback, and Voice conference control (Enterprise/Twilio).

tags.name: Account, Profile, Auth & Notifications
tags.description: Manage Chat SPX accounts (signup, settings, custom attributes, chat wallpaper, billing/limits), the authenticated user profile (details, password, avatar, availability, UI settings, MFA), SAML SSO authentication, and per-account notifications, notification settings and push subscriptions. Unless noted, endpoints authenticate with the user access token sent in the `api_access_token` header; account-scoped routes additionally require the caller to be a member of the target account.

tags.name: Platform API
tags.description: Provider/administration APIs for Chat SPX. A **Platform App** uses these endpoints to provision and manage accounts, users, account memberships (account users), agent bots, and to migrate email channels in bulk. All requests authenticate with a Platform App access token sent in the `api_access_token` header. A Platform App can only act on the resources it owns (its *permissibles*): trying to read or mutate a resource that was not created by — or associated with — the calling Platform App returns `401 Unauthorized`.

tags.name: Public API (Inboxes & Help Center)
tags.description: Unauthenticated client/widget endpoints used by chat clients and the public Help Center of Chat SPX. The inbox endpoints let an end-user (contact) create themselves on an API channel inbox, open conversations, exchange messages, manage typing/last-seen/resolution, and submit CSAT replies — all keyed by the inbox identifier and the contact source_id (plus an optional HMAC identity hash). The Help Center endpoints under /hc expose portals, categories and articles for public reading and search. None of these routes require an API key; access is scoped implicitly by the inbox identifier or the portal slug.

tags.name: Live Chat Widget API
tags.description: Endpoints consumed by the **Chat SPX Live Chat Widget** (the JavaScript chat bubble embedded on a website) to bootstrap a session, identify the visitor (contact), exchange messages and run campaigns. These are *client-side* endpoints called directly from the visitor's browser, so they do **not** use the agent `api_access_token`. Authentication is two-layered: (1) a public **`website_token`** query parameter that identifies the Web Widget channel/inbox, and (2) a signed **`X-Auth-Token`** JWT header that authenticates the visitor's contact session. The JWT is minted by `POST /api/v1/widget/config` and returned as `website_channel_config.auth_token`; it encodes the `source_id` (contact inbox) and `inbox_id`. Endpoints that only need the channel (`/config`, `/campaigns`, `/inbox_members`) require just the `website_token`; all contact-scoped endpoints additionally require the `X-Auth-Token` header. Timestamps in widget responses are Unix epoch seconds and conversation/message ids are the per-account `display_id`.

Passing `assignee_id` null/0 unassigns. Manual assignment of a Captain mirror bot is admin-only (403) and the assistant must be eligible for the inbox (422). Validates the Private Chat password and, on success, returns a short-lived JWT used as the Bearer token for the Private Chat message endpoints. Authenticated with the standard `api_access_token`.

post.description: Sets the current actor's reaction on the message. A user (or contact) can hold only one reaction per message: reacting with a new emoji replaces the previous one, while re-sending the same emoji is an idempotent no-op. Only the curated emoji set is accepted. Returns `201 Created` for a brand-new reaction and `200 OK` when an existing reaction was updated or unchanged.

200.description: Existing reaction updated to a new emoji, or unchanged (idempotent).

422.description: Emoji is blank, too long, or outside the allowed set (`{"error":"invalid_emoji"}`).

Two mutually-exclusive selection modes: pass `attachment_ids` for an explicit selection, or pass `filters` (optionally with `conversation_id`) to grab everything matching the gallery filter / whole conversation. Limits: at most 500 files and 2 GB total; only one active export per user at a time (retained for 7 days). Returns `202 Accepted` with the new export record.
